_provenance: July 2026 analysis outputs. Cohort and diagnosis counts use distinct children in annotated_psychiatric_data_complete.csv. The full-cohort regression uses Mv_logit_readmission.csv. The 1,569-child predictions and error-rate comparisons use AdvStats_optimism_validation.csv and AdvStats_fairness_disparities.csv. The broader subgroup comparisons use Subgroup_AUC.csv. tools/refresh_portfolio_data.py reproduces these aggregates from the local analysis files.

pipeline.t: Group ICD-10-CM codes by diagnosis. Count each child once in each category, including diagnoses recorded in more than one field.
Estimate adjusted odds ratios for 90-day readmission using logistic regression across the full cohort.
Compare logistic regression, random forest and CatBoost using held-out predictions. Examine calibration and differences in error rates across patient groups.

groups.insurance_note: 39 children with missing insurance were excluded.
groups.cssrs_note: 414 children with only a yellow or orange flag were excluded.

spectrum.prose_note: Each bar shows the percentage of children with that diagnosis who returned within 90 days. A child can appear in more than one group.

models.clinical_read: Among the 1,569 children with a recorded ACE score, logistic regression had the highest held-out AUC (0.660), followed by random forest (0.637) and CatBoost (0.590).
models.coding_note: The study mapping includes suicidal ideation (R45.851) in the self-injury code group. Of 966 children with that visit or chronic diagnosis flag, 965 also had R45.851. The two coefficients cannot distinguish the effects of suicidal ideation and non-suicidal self-injury.

equity.metric_note: The error-rate comparison used the 1,569 children with recorded adverse childhood experience (ACE) data. Of these children, 140 returned within 90 days.

figures.title: Cohort characteristics
figures.caption: Readmission counts and length of stay are shown for all 2,652 children. An adverse childhood experiences (ACE) score was recorded for 1,569.

figures.title: Readmission by patient group
figures.caption: Bars show observed rates with approximate 95% confidence intervals. The screening panel uses any C-SSRS flag. The insurance panel compares AHCCCS with all other records, including 39 with missing insurance.

figures.title: Readmission by diagnostic category
figures.caption: Each child counts once per category. The suicidal ideation / self-harm group includes ICD-10-CM R45.851.

figures.title: Adjusted odds of readmission
figures.caption: Eight selected terms from a 17-predictor logistic regression in 2,652 children. Of 966 children with the visit or chronic self-injury flag, 965 also had the suicidal-ideation code.

figures.title: ROC curves for held-out predictions
figures.caption: Ten-fold predictions for 2,652 children, including those with imputed ACE scores. The curves show how sensitivity and false-positive rates change with the alert threshold. Imputation and scaling were fitted before the folds were split.

figures.title: Model validation estimates
figures.caption: In 1,569 children with a recorded ACE score, 140 were readmitted. The figure compares training, bootstrap-corrected and held-out AUC. Random forest and CatBoost also underwent nested cross-validation.

figures.title: Model error rates by subgroup
figures.caption: The analysis selected one logistic regression threshold (0.078) from the validation sample and used it for every group. Gender identity was recorded at admission. The insurance comparison uses recorded AHCCCS versus other or missing insurance.

figures.title: Flagging thresholds and workload
figures.caption: Ten-fold predictions in the full cohort of 2,652 children. Sensitivity is the share of readmitted children flagged. Positive predictive value is the share of flagged children who returned. Each dotted line marks where false alarms and missed readmissions were closest within the range tested for that model.

figures.title: Training and held-out AUC
figures.caption: Training, bootstrap-corrected and held-out AUC for the 1,569 children with a recorded ACE score.

figures.title: Feature importance by model
figures.caption: Models fitted to all 2,652 children. Random forest importance measures reductions in node impurity. CatBoost importance measures changes in predictions. The self-injury code group includes suicidal ideation.

figures.title: SHAP values for CatBoost
figures.caption: For the CatBoost model fitted to 2,652 children, positive SHAP values raise the model score and negative values lower it. The self-injury code group includes suicidal ideation.

figures.title: Calibration curves
figures.caption: Full cohort of 2,652 children. Each point compares the average held-out prediction with the observed readmission rate in one of ten groups ordered by predicted risk. The histograms show where the model scores fall.

sections.body: We examined which features of a psychiatric admission were associated with a child’s return to the hospital within 90 days and how accurately clinical records predicted that return.

We reviewed admissions from 2017 through 2024 for 2,652 children aged 5–12 at one Arizona hospital. We grouped diagnoses using ICD-10-CM codes and fitted a multivariable logistic regression. For 1,569 children with recorded ACE data, we compared three prediction models using 10-fold cross-validation and bootstrap correction.

Within 90 days, 246 children (9.3%) returned. Higher adjusted odds of readmission were associated with depressive disorders (OR 1.69, 95% CI 1.18–2.41), each additional diagnostic category (OR 1.34, 1.19–1.52) and physical restraint use (OR 1.55, 1.08–2.21). Older age was associated with lower odds (OR 0.91 per year, 0.84–0.99). The study’s self-injury code group included suicidal ideation, which limited interpretation of those two coefficients. Held-out AUC ranged from 0.590 to 0.660. At the common threshold, logistic regression flagged 82.1% of readmitted children aged 5–9 and 56.2% of those aged 10–12.

Several admission characteristics were associated with a return to the same hospital. Even the best-performing model had limited ability to distinguish individual children who returned from those who did not. How well these estimates apply at other hospitals remains unknown.

objectives.t: Identify clinical characteristics associated with 90-day readmission after adjustment for other recorded factors.
Interpret a difference between training and held-out AUC and explain what it means for individual predictions.
Compare missed readmissions and false alerts across age and recorded gender groups.
